cards.text: Ai is a heap of ruins. At that time, Joshua, Israel's leader, builds an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal. Now you might think this was Joshua's own idea, but hold that thought.

cards.question: Why does Joshua build an altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal?

answers.text: It marked the win at Ai

cards.text: Moses, the servant of the LORD, left instructions in the Book of the Law, and Joshua builds it exactly by the Book. He is NOT one of those "I don't need the instructions" guys.

cards.question: Joshua builds it the way the Book of the Law says: an altar of ___ stones, with no iron tool used on them.
On the altar of uncut stones at Mount Ebal, the Israelites offer burnt offerings and peace offerings.

cards.text: Then, right there in front of all the Israelites, Joshua starts writing on the stones. Not a doodle. Not a "Joshua was here."

cards.question: What does Joshua write on the stones at Mount Ebal?

answers.text: A copy of the law of Moses
The names of the twelve tribes
A record of the battle at Ai

cards.text: Now picture the crowd. ALL Israel, with their elders, officers and judges, stands on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carry it.
Then the crowd splits down the middle. Half stand in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, like an usher at a wedding going, "Bride's side or groom's side?" times a WHOLE nation.

cards.question: In the crowd standing around the ark, there are citizens of Israel but no foreigners.
Moses had commanded this two-mountain setup earlier, so they could ___ the people of Israel.

cards.text: Afterward, Joshua takes the words of the law and reads them OUT LOUD to the whole crowd, according to what's written in the Book of the Law.

cards.question: When Joshua reads the law aloud, he reads the blessings and leaves out the curses.

cards.text: Not one word of all Moses commanded gets skipped. Friend, I skipped ONE line on a recipe card once and baked a tray of hockey pucks, so Joshua's got my respect.

cards.question: Joshua reads every word Moses commanded to the whole assembly. Besides the foreigners, who does the text make a point of naming there?

answers.text: The women and the little ones

findings.problem: The wrong answer "It marked the win at Ai" isn't shown false anywhere in the passage. The altar is built "at that time," right after Ai, and the text never rules out that it marked the win. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: A baker could argue for "It marked the win at Ai" because of the timing in 8:30, so it should be replaced.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 8 lists the crowd as "ALL Israel, with their elders, officers and judges" and leaves out the foreigners. That steers the baker toward True, which is the wrong answer. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason that foreigners were there.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "Who does the text make a point of naming there?" sounds like a test question about the text. It should sound like Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.
